dedupe_keys.name: ei 3 fossil fuel energy infrastructure point dataset and nearby population counts for the contiguous us buonocore et al erl 2025

description: A national dataset, [EI]3, of 25 types of fossil fuel energy infrastructure across the supply chain with counts and demographics of people living nearby, built at Boston University and published with an Environmental Research Letters article in 2025. Contents: point locations of 1,217,957 infrastructure elements from federal sources such as HIFLD and the EIA, including 1,866 gas pipeline compressor stations and 31 gas import and export terminals in the transportation stage, with 2020 census block populations within 800 m and 1.6 km buffers. About 46.6 million people, 14.1 percent of the contiguous US population, live within 1.6 km of at least one element, with racial and ethnic disparities at nearly every stage. Coverage: contiguous United States. Format and access: the data are on Harvard Dataverse (doi 10.7910/DVN/KLUSQB). Licence (read on 2026-09-29): CC0-1.0 (Harvard Dataverse record); article CC-BY-4.0. Access is free of charge. Caveats: pipelines themselves, gathering equipment and distribution lines are left out, and federal sources may undercount elements such as compressor stations. Useful for hazard exposure and equity analysis of pipeline facilities. It relates to the EIA compressor station report and the proposed gas pipelines environmental justice case study in the catalogue.
